item.title: Justice B.R. Gavai, former CJI, appointed as Dr B.R. Ambedkar Chair Professor on Constitutional Law at NALSAR Hyderabad
item.description: Justice B.R. Gavai, former Chief Justice of India, has been appointed as the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Chair Professor on Constitutional Law and Social Inclusion at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad. The post Justice B.R. Gavai, former CJI, appointed as Dr B.R. Ambedkar Chair Professor on Constitutional Law at NALSAR Hyderabad appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas is acting as Indian legal counsel to PTC Inc. on the sale of its Kepware and ThingWorx businesses
item.description: The transaction involves multidisciplinary legal advice spanning M&A, employment, tax, data privacy, and equity compensation matters. The post Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas is acting as Indian legal counsel to PTC Inc. on the sale of its Kepware and ThingWorx businesses appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Intra-court appeal not maintainable in patent disputes; Commercial Courts Act overrides Letters Patent of High Court: Madras High Court
item.description: “Any expansion of the scope of the Commercial Courts Act would defeat its objectives, and there is no ambiguity regarding appeals from decrees of Commercial Courts and Commercial Divisions under Section 13 of the Commercial Courts Act.” The post Intra-court appeal not maintainable in patent disputes; Commercial Courts Act overrides Letters Patent of High Court: Madras High Court appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Continued online circulation of arrest reports after discharge violates Right to Dignity; Delhi High Court upholds interim de-indexing against Media House
item.description: While the media enjoys freedom of speech and expression, but such right is not absolute and stands correspondingly delimited by the right of an individual to dignity and reputation. The post Continued online circulation of arrest reports after discharge violates Right to Dignity; Delhi High Court upholds interim de-indexing against Media House appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: ‘Financial debt exceeded minimum threshold’: NCLT admits insolvency application against Sparklet Engineers Private Ltd.
item.description: Although the respondent acknowledged execution of works, instalments under the Vendor Settlement Agreement remained unpaid. With repeated acknowledgments of inability to pay and only the first tranche settled, default was established under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The post ‘Financial debt exceeded minimum threshold’: NCLT admits insolvency application against Sparklet Engineers Private Ltd. appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co. advises Nephrocare Health Services Limited on its Initial Public Offering
item.description: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas advised Nephrocare Health Services Limited (Nephroplus) on its initial public offering aggregating to approximately US$ 95.99 million, covering Indian law, regulatory compliance, and prospectus and listing support. The post Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co. advises Nephrocare Health Services Limited on its Initial Public Offering appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: “More than 16 years have passed but this project is still slow in progress”: Read why Allahabad HC issued directions for implementation of Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System
item.description: “ICJS has been established to make justice delivery system more effective by integrating main pillars of criminal justice, i.e., the police (CCTNS), courts (e-courts), jails (e-prisons), forensic lab (e-forensic) and prosecution (e-prosecution).” The post “More than 16 years have passed but this project is still slow in progress”: Read why Allahabad HC issued directions for implementation of Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Appellate Deposit under Section 148 NI Act: Whether can be directed against Convicted Director or Confined to Juristic Drawer? Supreme Court Larger Bench to Decide
item.description: Section 148 NI Act was introduced to remedy the systemic abuse of appellate processes, whereby convicted drawers routinely secured suspension of sentence and delayed payment of compensation for years, thereby frustrating the object of Section 138 of NI Act. The post Appellate Deposit under Section 148 NI Act: Whether can be directed against Convicted Director or Confined to Juristic Drawer? Supreme Court Larger Bench to Decide appeared first on SCC Times.
